- Avoid over-optimistic spikes in forecasts when sentiment is neutral or flat; true prices often correct downward after sharp upward moves.
- When recent history shows strong upward momentum, model should not over-forecast the next 30-day peak; mean reversion toward prior 10-15 day average is common.
- If forecasted price exceeds true outcome by >5% in 3 consecutive days, reduce subsequent forecast by 1-2% to avoid overshoot bias.
- For neutral sentiment history, model should not assume continuation of recent trend; instead, anchor forecast to 14-day moving average or 30-day median.
- If true outcome shows early “reversal” (e.g., 3-day drop after 5-day rise), model should adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% in next 5-day window to avoid lagged reaction.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), avoid forecasting volatility; use smoothing filters or conservative drift models to prevent overreaction to noise.
